A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 29-page versions of the same study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–J are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original measurements of representation dimensionality, training dynamics and correlations with dataset complexity on controlled grammars and The Pile, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains the original dimensionality measurements, training-dynamics analyses and complexity correlations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The representation-analysis procedure is retained: last-token residual representations, TwoNN intrinsic dimension, PCA effective dimension and gzip-based complexity estimation. The expanded explanations do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same controlled grammars, coupling and shuffling conditions, sequence lengths, The Pile and Appendix F benchmarks. The new systems A/B example in Section 3.1 is illustrative, not an additional evaluation dataset.

E2.justification: The evaluated Pythia, Llama and Mistral models and alternative dimensionality estimators MLE and Participation Ratio are retained. Newly cited works and the GPT-4 vocabulary disclosure introduce no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported splits, sample sizes, representation extraction, 99% PCA variance threshold and zero-shot benchmark protocol remain unchanged. Appendix E adds preparation details without stating that the existing experimental settings changed.

E4.justification: The same coupling, shuffling, sequence-length, alternative-estimator and rogue-dimension analyses remain. Figure 4's plotted-result adjustments do not introduce a new ablation, control or diagnostic question.

E5.justification: Both retain five-split/seed reporting, means with one standard deviation, regression statistics and Spearman significance thresholds. No repeated-run count or uncertainty-estimation practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figure 4's lower-right PCA difference panel revises some late-training plotted points, notably the coherent 410m and 1.4b endpoints. Table 1, Tables G.1, H.1 and I.1, and the other figures retain their results. The principal trends remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The estimator assumptions and equations, dimensionality definitions and grammar-sampling mathematics are retained. The dimensionality inequality omitted from the main text remains in Appendices D and G. Section 3.1 adds an intuitive example rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same principal claims: different linear/nonlinear scaling, a training transition linked to linguistic competence, and complementary encoding of superficial and meaningful compositional complexity.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly explains wordform complexity as a competing interpretation motivating the shuffling control. It also drops v3's assertion that processing unlikely-to-be-memorized sentences necessarily requires successful compositional generalization. The main mechanism interpretation and limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project code link beneath the abstract. Appendix E.6 newly documents GPT-4 vocabulary generation, example prompts, conditioning on previous lists and replacement of duplicates. The vocabulary tables, hardware and computation-time disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 refocuses compositionality background on sample-, system- and model-level perspectives, adding works including Brighton and Kirby, Chaabouni et al., Hupkes et al. and Partee while removing several earlier capability and interpretability citations. The closest geometry comparisons and novelty claims remain.

P1.justification: Targeted rewriting clarifies Background and Setup, adds Section 3.1, moves Models after Datasets and relocates the memorization discussion to Appendix E. Terminology and prose are polished, and a co-first-author note is added; the overall results and discussion structure remains.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with distinct model-series colors, revised panel spacing, axes and separators. Section 3.1 adds a compact A/B example display. Other changes mainly concern sizing and text flow; the existing numbered figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves clarity about the system-level compositionality being studied and strengthens reproducibility documentation through the code link and GPT-4 vocabulary instructions. It also removes an overly categorical generalization assertion. Figure 4's small unexplained trace adjustments temper the gain, but the principal evidence and conclusions remain stable.
